stacks.description:
An ASP.NET Core Web API with controllers on the current long-term-support .NET, and an xUnit test project.

- `Directory.Build.props` at the tier root marks the tier and holds the build settings every project shares (target framework, nullable reference types, warnings as errors).
- `src/Api/` is the API project, `tests/Api.Tests/` its tests; the solution file at the tier root holds both.
- Packages go to the API project (`addPackage`) or to the test project (`addDevPackage`).
A Flutter app for Android, iOS and web. Recipes add capabilities behind small Dart interfaces (ports), with a mock adapter for tests and a real adapter for production.
A TypeScript HTTP API on Express, with tsoa controllers. Recipes add infrastructure (errors, logging, configuration, repositories, security guards) as small modules with interfaces.
A React single-page app built with Vite and TypeScript, for admin and back-office screens.

scaffolds.description:
An Express API with tsoa controllers.

- `src/server.ts` builds the app: middleware first, then `RegisterRoutes(app)` from `src/generated/routes.ts`.
- `src/index.ts` starts the server on `PORT`.
- Controllers live in `src/features/<feature>/presentation/controllers/*Controller.ts`; `tsoa.json` finds them there. One health controller answers `GET /health`.
- `npm run generate` writes the routes and the OpenAPI spec to `src/generated/` (not committed). `build`, `lint` and `test` run it first.
- `npm run test` runs every `src/**/*.test.ts` file with the Node test runner and `tsx`, without a separate build.

notes: The scaffold is an Express and tsoa API: `tsoa.json`, `src/server.ts` (the app), `src/index.ts` (starts it), a health controller, and routes generated before every build, lint and test.
TypeScript tests run directly with `node --import tsx --test`; the scaffold ships one for `GET /health`.

meta.name: ASP.NET Core Foundation (Problem Details, Typed Settings, Health Checks)

recipes.description: The base the other C# recipes build on: an exception taxonomy (`AppException` with `InvalidInputException`, `ForbiddenException`, `NotFoundException`, `ConflictException`) answered as RFC 9457 problem details by one `IExceptionHandler`, typed settings bound from the `Api` section and validated at startup (`ApiOptions`), and a readiness endpoint `GET /health/ready` from ASP.NET Core health checks. An unexpected exception is logged and answered with 500 without its message.

instructions.instruction: Add `using Api.Core;` at the top. After `builder.Services.AddControllers();`, call `builder.Services.AddCoreFoundation(builder.Configuration);`. Right after `var app = builder.Build();`, call `app.UseCoreFoundation();`.

conventions.rule: Signal an expected failure by throwing one of the `AppException` types from `Api.Core.Errors`; never build error responses by hand in a controller. Settings a service needs go into an options class with data annotations, bound and validated like `ApiOptions`, and are read through `IOptions<T>`.

meta.name: Node.js HMAC Request Body Tamper Guard Extension

recipes.description:
Cryptographic HMAC-SHA256 signature verification extension for API requests. Guarantees message integrity, replay protection with timestamp freshness windows, and payload tamper defense.

The shared signing secret is read from the `HMAC_SECRET_KEY` environment variable (or passed as `secretKey`); a request fails when neither is set.

notes: The signing secret comes only from `HMAC_SECRET_KEY` (or `secretKey`) at run time; the `HMAC_SECRET_KEY` parameter, which wrote the secret into the source file, is removed.
Removed the `HMAC_VERIFICATION_DISABLED` switch that skipped verification.
No `extensions/index.ts`: it replaced the App Check recipe's file of the same name; import the verifier from its own file.

instructions.instruction: Import HmacSignatureVerifier from './extensions/HmacSignatureVerifier' and invoke 'HmacSignatureVerifier.verify(request)' inside the expressAuthentication hook, before the scheme is resolved, to protect endpoints against tampering and replay attacks.

meta.name: Node.js TSOA Firebase Security Gateway & Multi-Tenant Auth

recipes.description:
Production TSOA expressAuthentication security gateway. Handles multi-app resolution (x-app-id), Firebase Bearer token verification, Admin RBAC roles from the token's `roles` custom claim, and pre-populates request.user with fully hydrated TenantInfo so controllers remain 100% auth-agnostic.

Firebase Admin uses the application default credentials (`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, or the platform's service account).

notes: Admin endpoints (`admin_rbac`) verify the Firebase token and require its `roles` claim to hold the scopes; any bearer token was accepted as an admin before.
A tenant is always resolved by the provider set at startup; `TokenTenantInfoProvider` is the shipped one. Without a provider the request fails instead of building a tenant from the token silently.
Instructions name the scaffold's files (`tsoa.json`, `createServer` in `src/server.ts`).

instructions.instruction: Add `"authenticationModule": "./src/core/auth/expressAuthentication.ts"` to the `routes` object, so the generated routes call `expressAuthentication` for every `@Security` decorator.

In `createServer`, before `RegisterRoutes(app)`, call `setTenantInfoProvider(new TokenTenantInfoProvider())`, importing both from `./core/auth`. A project whose tenants are stored records passes its own `ITenantInfoProvider` instead.
